extraction.name: IFEval: Instruction-Following Eval for Large Language Models
extraction.description: IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark for assessing the instruction-following ability of Large Language Models (LLMs). It focuses on a set of 25 types of 'verifiable instructions' such as 'write in more than 400 words' and 'mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times'. The benchmark consists of around 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions that can be objectively verified using simple, interpretable, and deterministic programs.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou (Google and Yale University)
extraction.citeAs: Zhou, J., Lu, T., Mishra, S., Brahma, S., Basu, S., Luan, Y., Zhou, D., & Hou, L. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a combination of few-shot prompting and manual curation. Base prompts were generated with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended to the end of each prompt. Few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical prompts, and another few-shot prompting approach was used to rephrase each prompt to increase diversity. Finally, all rephrased prompts were manually checked and edited one by one.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts combined with verifiable instructions, generated via few-shot prompting using large language models, followed by manual curation and editing.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompts were generated in four steps: (1) generate base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended; (2) use few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts; (3) apply few-shot prompting to rephrase each prompt to increase phrasing diversity; (4) manually check and edit each rephrased prompt.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Illogical prompts were identified and removed using few-shot prompting. Prompts were rephrased to increase diversity. All prompts were manually reviewed and edited. For evaluation, responses are transformed using up to eight transformation functions (e.g., removing markdown font modifiers, removing first/last lines) to compute loose accuracy and reduce false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Verification of instruction-following is performed automatically using deterministic programs. A strict metric checks if instructions are followed exactly, while a loose metric applies transformations (removing markdown tags, removing first/last lines of responses) to reduce false negatives. 25 types of verifiable instructions are defined, each with a corresponding programmatic verification function.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The evaluation uses both strict and loose accuracy metrics. Strict accuracy directly checks if instructions are followed. Loose accuracy applies up to eight response transformations to reduce false negatives, though this may introduce false positives. The loose criterion is considered a complement to the strict criterion. Results are reported at both prompt-level and instruction-level.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4, PaLM 2 Small (S) — used for few-shot prompting during prompt generation and for evaluation as baseline models. Deterministic programmatic verifiers are used for instruction-following verification.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code and data are released at https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/instruction_following_eval. Future work includes improving prompts and verifiable instructions, expanding to more verifiable instruction types, and supporting multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Ensuring that LLMs can consistently adhere to given directives is important for safety and reliability of LLM implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Human evaluations are noted to be potentially biased and inconsistent. Model-based evaluation can yield misleading signals if the evaluator model has significant limitations. The IFEval benchmark focuses on verifiable instructions to reduce subjectivity, but acknowledges that very few instructions are 100% objectively and automatically verifiable, and edge cases exist.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current set of verifiable instructions may not cover all real-world instruction types. Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically — edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The loose accuracy metric, while reducing false negatives, may introduce false positives. The benchmark currently does not support multi-modal use cases. The list of 25 verifiable instructions may not be fully representative of the diversity of real-world instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of the instruction-following ability of Large Language Models. The benchmark can be used to compare different LLMs on various instruction types, identify which types of instructions are not usually followed, and provide an automatic, reproducible, and objective evaluation of LLM instruction-following capabilities.
